<script>
  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

Discussion ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_title"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_ref">6.4 </span>Implications for Human–AI Interaction</span></a></li>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line ltx_leqno">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Hanjing Shi
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">email: </span><a href="mailto:hasa23@lehigh.edu">hasa23@lehigh.edu</a>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_institution">Lehigh University</span>, <span id="id2" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_city">Bethlehem</span>, <span id="id3" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_state">Pennsylvania</span>, <span id="id4" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_country">USA</span>
</span></span></span></span>
<span class="ltx_author_before"> and </span><span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Dominic DiFranzo
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">email: </span><a href="mailto:djd219@lehigh.edu">djd219@lehigh.edu</a>
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span><span id="id5" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_institution">Lehigh University</span>, <span id="id6" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_city">Bethlehem</span>, <span id="id7" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_state">Pennsylvania</span>, <span id="id8" class="ltx_text ltx_affiliation_country">USA</span>
</span></span></span></span></div>
<div class="ltx_dates">© none</div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract.</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Traditional AI alignment primarily focuses on individual model outputs; however, autonomous agents in long-horizon workflows require sustained reliability across entire interaction trajectories. We introduce <span id="abstract1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">APEMO</span> (Affect-aware Peak-End Modulation for Orchestration), a runtime scheduling layer that optimizes computational allocation under fixed budgets by operationalizing temporal-affective signals. Instead of modifying model weights, APEMO detects trajectory instability through behavioral proxies and targets repairs at critical segments, such as peak moments and endings. Evaluation across multi-agent simulations and LLM-based planner–executor flows demonstrates that APEMO consistently enhances trajectory-level quality and reuse probability over structural orchestrators. Our results reframe alignment as a temporal control problem, offering a resilient engineering pathway for the development of long-horizon agentic systems.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1. </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Artificial intelligence systems are rapidly transitioning from single-turn instruction followers to autonomous, multi-step agents operating within long-horizon workflows. Recent work on autonomous LLM agents has demonstrated sustained multi-step planning and open-ended interaction <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. In such environments, large language models (LLMs) plan, execute, and coordinate across specialized roles to solve open-ended tasks. Alignment in these settings is no longer solely a property of model parameters; it unfolds across time. System behavior accumulates over turns, and user expectations adapt throughout the interaction. Over extended trajectories, accumulated inconsistencies may lead to cumulative frustration or degradation of behavioral coherence.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Recent advances in AI alignment have focused on value specification and instruction tuning, particularly through reinforcement learning from human feedback (RLHF) <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christiano et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. In parallel, the HCI community has established principles for transparency, trust calibration, and effective human–AI collaboration <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">Amershi et al., 2019</a>; <a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">Bansal et al., 2021</a>)</cite>. These approaches primarily operate at the model or interface level. They improve output correctness, explanation quality, and interaction clarity. However, they do not explicitly address how alignment unfolds across extended interaction sequences.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">At the orchestration level, multi-agent and workflow frameworks have advanced structural optimization. Structured reasoning paradigms such as ReAct <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2022</a>)</cite> and automated workflow generation systems such as AFlow <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024</a>)</cite> focus on improving task accuracy, routing strategies, and computational efficiency. Yet these systems typically aggregate performance across steps. They rarely treat the temporal structure of interaction as an alignment variable. In long-horizon workflows, perceived reliability depends not only on average step correctness, but also on how systems recover from intermediate failures and how trajectories conclude.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Psychological research demonstrates that retrospective evaluations of experiences are temporally structured. The peak–end rule shows that judgments are disproportionately influenced by the most intense moment and the ending of an experience <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahneman et al., 1993</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fredrickson and Kahneman, 1993</a>)</cite>. This temporal asymmetry suggests that interaction quality cannot be fully captured by mean performance alone. If human evaluation is temporally weighted, then alignment mechanisms that ignore trajectory structure may systematically misalign with how users assess system reliability and reuse potential.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">In this paper, we introduce <span id="S1.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">APEMO</span> (Affect-aware Peak-End Modulation for Orchestration), a temporal-affective orchestration layer for AI workflows. APEMO does not modify model weights or training objectives. Instead, it reallocates reasoning effort and repair across a trajectory under fixed computational budgets. We formulate temporal orchestration as a constrained multi-objective optimization problem that balances trajectory-level quality, reuse propensity, frustration-related behavioral signals, and coordination cost.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Through systematic evaluation across long-horizon single-agent trajectories and multi-agent workflows, we investigate whether temporal control can function as a bidirectional alignment layer. Rather than aligning only token-level outputs to predefined values, our approach aligns interaction dynamics with evaluation-sensitive trajectory properties. This reframes alignment as a property of entire interaction sequences rather than isolated predictions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S1.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 1. Introduction ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> illustrates the core intuition of our approach.
Under uniform budget allocation, negative peaks persist and endings remain weak,
leading to trajectory-level instability. APEMO introduces temporal control that
detects and repairs negative peaks while preserving a fixed compute budget.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S1.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17910v1/workflow_apemo.png" id="S1.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/318;" width="476" height="318" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1. </span>
APEMO as a temporal-affective overlay for long-horizon workflows.
Uniform allocation optimizes mean-step performance but allows negative peaks to persist.
APEMO reallocates effort toward peak repair and ending stabilization under fixed compute budgets,
improving trajectory-level robustness.
</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2. </span>Related Work</h2>

<section id="S2.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.1. </span>Model Alignment and Preference Modeling</h3>

<div id="S2.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) aligns model outputs with human preferences by learning reward functions from labeled comparisons <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">Christiano et al., 2017</a>; <a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ouyang et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. However, human preference judgments are not temporally neutral. Prior work has shown that trajectory-level evaluations often exhibit non-Markovian structures, where judgments depend disproportionately on salient segments rather than average reward <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">Early et al., 2022</a>)</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Most alignment methods treat such temporal weighting as bias to be corrected within reward modeling. In contrast, our work treats temporal asymmetry as a structural signal. Rather than modifying the reward function or retraining the model, we operationalize evaluation-sensitive weighting at runtime. This shifts alignment from a parameter-level optimization problem to a trajectory-level control problem.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Recent work on self-reflection and iterative reasoning, such as Tree-of-Thoughts <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib16" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, Reflexion <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib17" title="" class="ltx_ref">Shinn and others, 2023</a>)</cite>, and Self-Refine <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib18" title="" class="ltx_ref">Madaan et al., 2023</a>)</cite>, improves performance by expanding search depth or introducing additional reasoning passes. These approaches typically increase computational effort to enhance solution quality. In contrast, APEMO operates under a fixed global budget and reallocates compute across turns. Our objective is not to increase total reasoning depth, but to redistribute effort toward evaluation-critical segments such as negative peaks and final states.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.2. </span>Agentic Orchestration and Multi-Agent Workflows</h3>

<div id="S2.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The field has rapidly progressed from single-step inference to compound AI systems composed of planners, executors, critics, and memory modules. ReAct interleaves reasoning and acting to improve task performance <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">Yao et al., 2022</a>)</cite>. AFlow automates agentic workflow generation using structured search <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2024</a>)</cite>. AgentOrchestra introduces hierarchical coordination via the Tool–Environment–Agent protocol <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">Zhang et al., 2025</a>)</cite>. More recent systems such as CORAL <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib14" title="" class="ltx_ref">Ren et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, Kairos <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib12" title="" class="ltx_ref">Chen et al., 2025</a>)</cite>, and Orchestrator <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib13" title="" class="ltx_ref">Beckenbauer et al., 2025</a>)</cite> address information flow, latency, and long-horizon coordination efficiency.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">These systems focus primarily on structural optimization, search efficiency, routing logic, or serving scalability. Their objectives typically aggregate performance across steps, implicitly approximating mean-step optimization. While some incorporate reflection or memory mechanisms, they rarely formalize temporal asymmetry as an optimization target. In particular, coordination cost is often treated as engineering overhead rather than an explicit trade-off variable.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Our work complements these orchestration architectures by introducing a temporal-affective overlay that operates orthogonally to workflow topology. Instead of redesigning agent roles or adding new modules, APEMO reallocates existing compute to stabilize evaluation-critical segments under a fixed budget. This distinguishes compute reallocation from compute expansion and frames coordination tax as a first-class variable in alignment analysis.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">2.3. </span>Temporal Evaluation and Robust Interaction Trajectories</h3>

<div id="S2.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The peak–end rule demonstrates that retrospective evaluations are disproportionately influenced by the most intense moment and the ending of an experience <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">Kahneman et al., 1993</a>; <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">Fredrickson and Kahneman, 1993</a>)</cite>. This temporal asymmetry suggests that interaction quality cannot be fully captured by mean performance alone. If human assessment is temporally weighted, then alignment mechanisms that optimize uniform step performance may systematically diverge from user-perceived reliability.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In long-horizon AI systems, extended interaction introduces additional challenges, including behavioral drift and coherence degradation over time. Open-ended agents such as Voyager illustrate how multi-step autonomy increases exposure to trajectory instability <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib15" title="" class="ltx_ref">Wang et al., 2023</a>)</cite>. Memory architectures such as BMAM provide mechanisms for salience-aware retrieval <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_citep">(<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">Li et al., 2026</a>)</cite>, yet memory storage alone does not specify how compute should be redistributed when instability arises.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">APEMO integrates temporal evaluation principles with runtime control by treating frustration-related behavioral proxies as actionable signals. Rather than enforcing uniform quality across all turns, it prioritizes negative-peak recovery and end-state stabilization under fixed computational constraints.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.SS3.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.SS3.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To validate this control principle across abstraction levels, we adopt a stacked evidence strategy spanning Agent-Based Modeling (ABM), single-agent LLM reasoning, and multi-agent workflows. ABM isolates temporal dynamics under controlled Monte Carlo sampling; single-agent LLM experiments test robustness under neural stochasticity; and multi-agent evaluations verify that temporal control remains orthogonal to role decomposition. Together, these layers demonstrate that peak-aware compute reallocation is not a simulation artifact but a transferable orchestration principle.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3. </span>Methodology</h2>

<section id="S3.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.1. </span>Problem Formulation</h3>

<div id="S3.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We model a long-horizon AI workflow as a trajectory of <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>T</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T</annotation></semantics></math> sequential turns.
At each turn <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the system produces an intermediate output <math id="S3.SS1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="y_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>y</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">y_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and generates observable behavioral signals.
Rather than optimizing isolated step accuracy, we treat alignment as a trajectory-level property.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">APEMO defines a runtime policy <math id="S3.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>π</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi</annotation></semantics></math> that maximizes the following constrained objective:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>

</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">where:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<ul id="S3.I1" class="ltx_itemize">
<li id="S3.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> denotes peak-end weighted trajectory quality,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math> denotes reuse-related robustness,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> denotes cumulative frustration burden,</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S3.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">•</span> 
<div id="S3.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.I1.i4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math> denotes coordination cost.</p>
</div></li>
</ul>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p6.1" class="ltx_p">All policies operate under identical model weights, decoding parameters, workflow topology, and shared computational caps. Realized coordination cost may differ by policy and is explicitly measured.
APEMO differs from baselines only in runtime temporal allocation and repair scheduling.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Trajectory-level quality <math id="S3.SS1.p7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math> is defined using peak-end weighting:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p8" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(2)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q=w_{p}\max(q_{1\dots T})+w_{e}\cdot\text{mean}(q_{T-1},q_{T})" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>Q</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>p</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.167em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">…</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>T</mi></mrow></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>+</mo><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mi>e</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">⋅</mo><mtext>mean</mtext></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>−</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>q</mi><mi>T</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q=w_{p}\max(q_{1\dots T})+w_{e}\cdot\text{mean}(q_{T-1},q_{T})</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p9" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p9.1" class="ltx_p">Coordination cost accumulates as:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p10" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_left"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_left">(3)</span></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C=C_{policy}+C_{repair}+C_{overhead}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>l</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>c</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>p</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>i</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi></mrow></msub><mo>+</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>o</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>v</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>r</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>h</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>e</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>d</mi></mrow></msub></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C=C_{policy}+C_{repair}+C_{overhead}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p11" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p11.1" class="ltx_p">with the global constraint:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p12" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.Ex1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\leq C_{max}" display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\leq C_{max}</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS1.p13" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS1.p13.1" class="ltx_p">This formulation reframes alignment as trajectory dynamics optimization rather than token-level correctness.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.2. </span>Runtime Control Mechanism</h3>

<div id="S3.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S3.F2" title="Figure 2 ‣ 3.2. Runtime Control Mechanism ‣ 3. Methodology ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">2</span></a> illustrates the APEMO internal control loop.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S3.F2" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17910v1/inside_flow.png" id="S3.F2.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/318;" width="476" height="318" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 2. </span>
APEMO internal control loop.
At each turn <math id="S3.F2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, a frustration signal <math id="S3.F2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{f}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{f}(t)</annotation></semantics></math> is computed from behavioral proxies.
If a negative peak is detected, a precision repair module reallocates compute
toward peak and ending turns.
Coordination cost accumulates under a fixed budget constraint <math id="S3.F2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C\leq C_{max}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>≤</mo><msub><mi>C</mi><mrow><mi>m</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>a</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>x</mi></mrow></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C\leq C_{max}</annotation></semantics></math>.
</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S3.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">At each turn, behavioral proxy signals are aggregated into a scalar frustration score <math id="S3.SS2.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{f}(t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>f</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{f}(t)</annotation></semantics></math>.
A peak-detection condition evaluates whether trajectory quality has entered a negative regime.
When triggered, a precision repair operation reallocates compute from low-impact turns to peak or terminal segments.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The repair process does not modify model weights or workflow topology.
Instead, it redistributes inference precision within the same global compute budget.
Budget enforcement ensures that total coordination cost remains bounded.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS2.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Unlike topology-based orchestrators, APEMO operates as a temporal overlay that adjusts when and where reasoning precision is applied.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">3.3. </span>Trade-off and Frontier Analysis</h3>

<div id="S3.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Because temporal scheduling introduces coordination overhead,
we analyze the trade-off between robustness gains and coordination cost.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Configurations are projected onto a Pareto frontier defined over <math id="S3.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(R,C)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>R</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>C</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(R,C)</annotation></semantics></math>.
A configuration is considered economically viable if improvements in reuse-related robustness exceed marginal coordination overhead.</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This analysis isolates whether trajectory-level stabilization justifies additional orchestration cost under fixed budgets.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4. </span>Experimental Setup</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate APEMO under controlled equal-budget conditions to isolate the effect of temporal-affective orchestration.
Our objective is not to optimize model training but to test whether runtime temporal control improves trajectory-level robustness.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">All experiments are conducted using locally deployed small-model LLM families, including <span id="S4.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">llama3.2:1b</span>, <span id="S4.p2.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">qwen2.5:1.5b</span>, and <span id="S4.p2.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">gemma2:2b</span>, executed through an Ollama-based runtime.
Prompt templates, decoding parameters, and sampling temperature are held constant across all conditions.
No fine-tuning, reward modification, or architectural changes are applied.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Long-horizon evaluation uses <math id="S4.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=8</annotation></semantics></math> turns to induce trajectory drift and potential negative peaks.
Short-horizon evaluation uses <math id="S4.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=2</annotation></semantics></math> to test whether improvements depend on extended context accumulation.
Multi-agent settings adopt a fixed Planner–Executor–Critic topology across all variants, with APEMO applied solely as a temporal overlay.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Baselines include uniform budget allocation (mean-step optimization), structured reflective orchestration (<span id="S4.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute</span> and <span id="S4.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute_reflect</span>), and role-based multi-agent flows without temporal reallocation (<span id="S4.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">flow_plain</span> and <span id="S4.p4.1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">flow_temporal</span>).
All policies are evaluated under the same runtime protocol and global budget constraints; realized token and orchestration costs are then compared directly.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p5.1" class="ltx_p">To evaluate recovery robustness, we introduce a controlled perturbation benchmark that injects mid-trajectory reasoning degradation to simulate negative peaks.
Recovery quality is measured as post-perturbation stabilization relative to pre-trap performance.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p6.1" class="ltx_p">Performance is evaluated using four trajectory-level metrics: peak-end weighted quality <math id="S4.p6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="Q" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>Q</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">Q</annotation></semantics></math>, reuse-related robustness <math id="S4.p6.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="R" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>R</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">R</annotation></semantics></math>, cumulative frustration <math id="S4.p6.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math>, and coordination cost <math id="S4.p6.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="C" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>C</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">C</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p7.1" class="ltx_p">We conduct both agent-based model (ABM) simulations and real LLM executions.
ABM simulations are used for mechanism calibration and stress testing, while small-model LLM experiments provide the primary quantitative evidence reported in the main Results section.
This separation avoids over-claiming from simulator-only dynamics while preserving a controlled mechanism-development layer.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1. </span>Primary Block Configuration Overview</h3>

<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S4.T1" title="Table 1 ‣ 4.1. Primary Block Configuration Overview ‣ 4. Experimental Setup ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> summarizes the main LLM blocks reported in Results, including run count and validity gate.</p>
</div>

</section>
<section id="S4.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.2. </span>Statistical Analysis</h3>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">All statistics are computed at the run level.
Each run corresponds to a fixed configuration defined by model, seed, policy, and trajectory length.
Episode-level metrics are aggregated within run to avoid pseudo-replication.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">For each metric, we report mean, standard deviation (std), and standard error (se).
Uncertainty is estimated using nonparametric bootstrap confidence intervals with 95% coverage via resampling over runs.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Pairwise comparisons are expressed as delta metrics:</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p4" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta=\text{Metric}_{\text{APEMO}}-\text{Metric}_{\text{Baseline}}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mtext>Metric</mtext><mtext>APEMO</mtext></msub><mo>−</mo><msub><mtext>Metric</mtext><mtext>Baseline</mtext></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta=\text{Metric}_{\text{APEMO}}-\text{Metric}_{\text{Baseline}}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p5.1" class="ltx_p">For each delta, we report the 95% bootstrap confidence interval.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p6" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p6.1" class="ltx_p">As a conservative small-sample robustness check, we additionally report two-sided sign-test p-values based on directional wins across runs. Key p-values are reported in the main Results text and full p-value tables are provided in block-level comparison files.
This nonparametric test avoids distributional assumptions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p7" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p7.1" class="ltx_p">Interpretation is gated by reliability validity.
For each block, we compute a <span id="S4.SS2.p7.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">no_fallback_rate</span>.
Blocks with incomplete validity are treated as directional evidence rather than primary statistical support.</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS2.p8" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p8.1" class="ltx_p">All comparisons are theory-driven and restricted to predefined trajectory-level objectives.
Primary endpoints were fixed before large-<math id="S4.SS2.p8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>n</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n</annotation></semantics></math> reruns.
These include mean quality, reuse probability, reuse-per-cost, average frustration,
and trap endpoint and rebound metrics.
We emphasize effect sizes and uncertainty intervals over binary significance claims.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5. </span>Results</h2>

<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We report results with a staged validation strategy progressing from controlled trajectory tests to perturbation recovery and multi-agent extensions. All statistics are computed at the run level. Reported intervals are nonparametric 95% bootstrap confidence intervals.</p>
</div>
<section id="S5.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.1. </span>Long-Horizon Trajectory Performance</h3>

<div id="S5.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We first evaluate APEMO under strict long-horizon settings (<math id="S5.SS1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=8" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>8</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=8</annotation></semantics></math>) with cross-model runs and <math id="S5.SS1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=20</annotation></semantics></math> independent configurations. All runs completed without fallback (no_fallback_rate = 1.0).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to the peak-end baseline, APEMO improves mean trajectory quality by <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0791" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0791</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0791</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0525, 0.1055], sign-test <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=4.01\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4.01</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=4.01\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>) and reuse probability by <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0609" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0609</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0609</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0383, 0.0826], <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=4.01\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4.01</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=4.01\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>). Average frustration decreases by <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0172" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0172</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0172</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [-0.0306, -0.0071], <math id="S5.SS1.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.115" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.115</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.115</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to the affect baseline, gains are larger: quality <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1874" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1874</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1874</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.1596, 0.2159], <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1.91\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1.91</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1.91\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>), reuse probability <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1161" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1161</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1161</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0861, 0.1433], <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=4.01\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>4.01</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=4.01\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>), and frustration <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0543" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0543</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0543</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [-0.0805, -0.0356], <math id="S5.SS1.p3.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1.91\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1.91</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1.91\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS1.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p4.1" class="ltx_p">Table <a href="#S5.T2" title="Table 2 ‣ 5.1. Long-Horizon Trajectory Performance ‣ 5. <div id="S5.SS1.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS1.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F3" title="Figure 3 ‣ 5.1. Long-Horizon Trajectory Performance ‣ 5. Results ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">3</span></a> reports effect sizes and confidence intervals across long-horizon, short-horizon, trap, and multi-agent blocks.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F3" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17910v1/fig_forest_effects.png" id="S5.F3.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/243;" width="476" height="243" alt="Refer to caption">

</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS2" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.2. </span>ABM Mechanism Consistency (Support Layer)</h3>

<div id="S5.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To verify mechanism consistency beyond specific model families, we run high-volume ABM stress tests under matched policy structure. ABM results are directionally aligned with LLM findings (better endpoint/recovery behavior with lower frustration), supporting the control mechanism itself rather than any single LLM idiosyncrasy.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Because simulator effect magnitudes can be inflated relative to real LLM stochastic regimes, we treat ABM as support-layer evidence and report full ABM effect tables in supplementary material rather than using them as the primary basis of claims.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.3. </span>Short-Horizon Regime Boundary</h3>

<div id="S5.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">To test horizon sensitivity, we evaluate short-horizon runs (<math id="S5.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="T=2" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>T</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">T=2</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=21" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>21</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=21</annotation></semantics></math>, no_fallback_rate = <math id="S5.SS3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">APEMO improves mean quality by <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0520" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0520</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0520</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0303, 0.0750], <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0072</annotation></semantics></math>) and reuse probability by <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0613" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0613</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0613</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0339, 0.0910], <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0072" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0072</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0072</annotation></semantics></math>) over task_peak_end. Reuse-per-cost remains positive (<math id="S5.SS3.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0051" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0051</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0051</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0015, 0.0085], <math id="S5.SS3.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0266" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0266</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0266</annotation></semantics></math>), though effect magnitudes are smaller than in long-horizon settings.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This boundary condition suggests that coordination overhead amortizes more effectively when trajectories are deeper, consistent with the trajectory-level control hypothesis developed in Discussion.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.4. </span>Negative-Peak Perturbation and Recovery</h3>

<div id="S5.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We introduce controlled negative-peak perturbations (<math id="S5.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=20</annotation></semantics></math>, no_fallback_rate = <math id="S5.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">APEMO improves endpoint delivery quality by <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1243" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1243</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1243</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0522, 0.1924], <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0118" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0118</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0118</annotation></semantics></math>) relative to task_peak_end. Rebound metrics remain directionally positive but variance-sensitive: trap_quality_rebound2 <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0807" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0807</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0807</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0075, 0.1540], <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.824" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.824</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.824</annotation></semantics></math>), while trap_frustration_drop2 <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0439" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0439</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0439</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [-0.0084, 0.0943], <math id="S5.SS4.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.263" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.263</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.263</annotation></semantics></math>) includes zero. The CI and sign-test discrepancy on rebound is expected under this conservative test with mixed directional wins.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS4.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS4.p3.1" class="ltx_p">These results indicate that endpoint stabilization is robust, whereas intermediate rebound amplitudes depend more heavily on stochastic cross-model dynamics. Figure <a href="#S5.F4" title="Figure 4 ‣ 5.4. Negative-Peak Perturbation and Recovery ‣ 5. Results ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">4</span></a> shows trap-response dynamics. APEMO shows weaker quality collapse at the trap turn and improved endpoint recovery behavior.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F4" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.17910v1/fig_trap_recovery.png" id="S5.F4.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_landscape" style="aspect-ratio:476/223;" width="476" height="223" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 4. </span>Trap recovery dynamics in the <math id="S5.F4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=20" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>20</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=20</annotation></semantics></math> LLM trap block, derived from episode-level trap drop/rebound metrics. Left: quality change around trap; right: frustration change around trap. Shaded areas are 95% bootstrap CIs.</figcaption>
</figure>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS5" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.5. </span>Multi-Agent Workflow Extension</h3>

<div id="S5.SS5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We extend APEMO above a Planner–Executor–Critic topology (<math id="S5.SS5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=16" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>16</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=16</annotation></semantics></math>, no_fallback_rate = <math id="S5.SS5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="1.0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mn>1.0</mn><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">1.0</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to plain multi-agent flow, APEMO improves quality by <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1782" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1782</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1782</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.1386, 0.2132], <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=3.05\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>3.05</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=3.05\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>) and reuse probability by <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1257" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1257</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1257</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0869, 0.1633], <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=5.19\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5.19</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=5.19\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>). Relative to the stronger temporal-flow baseline, quality remains positive (<math id="S5.SS5.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0609" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0609</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0609</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0285, 0.0956], <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0768" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0768</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0768</annotation></semantics></math>) while reuse and reuse-per-cost are near ties (confidence intervals include zero; <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.4545" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.4545</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.4545</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S5.SS5.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.8036" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.8036</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.8036</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">This pattern suggests that temporal-affective scheduling complements structural role decomposition and yields its strongest improvements when no prior temporal control is present.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS6" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.6. </span>Plan-Execute-Class Baseline Alignment (L3)</h3>

<div id="S5.SS6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We expanded L3 to a larger cross-model block with <math id="S5.SS6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="n=30" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>n</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>30</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">n=30</annotation></semantics></math> valid turn-2 runs.
We compare plan_execute, plan_execute_reflect,
task_peak_end, and APEMO under the same runtime protocol.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to <span id="S5.SS6.p2.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute</span>, APEMO improves quality by <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1028" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1028</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1028</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0843, 0.1218], <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1.86\times 10^{-9}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1.86</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1.86\times 10^{-9}</annotation></semantics></math>), reuse probability by <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0547" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0547</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0547</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0381, 0.0724], <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=5.95\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5.95</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=5.95\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>), and reduces frustration by <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0181" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0181</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0181</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [-0.0269, -0.0105], <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=3.25\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>3.25</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=3.25\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>). Reuse-per-cost is also positive (<math id="S5.SS6.p2.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0027" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0027</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0027</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0006, 0.0048], <math id="S5.SS6.p2.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0428" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0428</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0428</annotation></semantics></math>).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Relative to <span id="S5.SS6.p3.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute_reflect</span>, APEMO remains positive on quality (<math id="S5.SS6.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0370" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0370</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0370</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0229, 0.0521], <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=5.95\times 10^{-5}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>5.95</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=5.95\times 10^{-5}</annotation></semantics></math>) and reuse probability (<math id="S5.SS6.p3.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0211" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0211</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0211</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0081, 0.0347], <math id="S5.SS6.p3.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0052" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0052</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0052</annotation></semantics></math>), while reuse-per-cost and frustration remain near ties (confidence intervals include zero).</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p4" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p4.1" class="ltx_p">To address long-horizon external-baseline alignment directly, we further run an L3 turn-8 cross-model block (<span id="S5.SS6.p4.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">n</span>=18, no_fallback_rate = 1.0). Relative to <span id="S5.SS6.p4.1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute</span>, APEMO improves mean quality by <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1259" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1259</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1259</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0987, 0.1521], <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=7.63\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>7.63</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=7.63\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>), reuse probability by <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1223" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1223</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1223</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.0857, 0.1573], <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1.45\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1.45</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1.45\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>), and average frustration by <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0193" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0193</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0193</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [-0.0295, -0.0100], <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0013" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0013</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0013</annotation></semantics></math>). Relative to <span id="S5.SS6.p4.1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">plan_execute_reflect</span>, quality remains positive at <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.1881" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.1881</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.1881</annotation></semantics></math> (95% CI [0.1557, 0.2247], <math id="S5.SS6.p4.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=7.63\times 10^{-6}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>7.63</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>6</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=7.63\times 10^{-6}</annotation></semantics></math>), with reuse and reuse-per-cost also positive.</p>
</div>
<div id="S5.SS6.p5" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS6.p5.1" class="ltx_p">Against <span id="S5.SS6.p5.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">task_peak_end</span> at turn-8, APEMO still improves quality (<math id="S5.SS6.p5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="+0.0988" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>+</mo><mn>0.0988</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">+0.0988</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [0.0631, 0.1356], <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=1.45\times 10^{-4}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1.45</mn><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=1.45\times 10^{-4}</annotation></semantics></math>) and frustration (<math id="S5.SS6.p5.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="-0.0096" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo>−</mo><mn>0.0096</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">-0.0096</annotation></semantics></math>, 95% CI [-0.0159, -0.0047], <math id="S5.SS6.p5.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="p=0.0075" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>p</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>0.0075</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">p=0.0075</annotation></semantics></math>), while reuse and reuse-per-cost become near ties. This reinforces the earlier boundary: L3 supports directional orthogonality, but efficiency deltas remain baseline-sensitive.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S5.SS7" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">5.7. </span>Coordination Frontier</h3>

<div id="S5.SS7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We quantify trade-offs between robustness and orchestration cost using relative quality gain and realized total coordination cost increase under shared runtime constraints.</p>
</div>

<div id="S5.SS7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.SS7.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F5" title="Figure 5 ‣ 5.7. Coordination Frontier ‣ 5. Results ‣ Alignment in Time: Peak-Aware Orchestration for Long-Horizon Agentic Systems" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">5</span></a> visualizes the frontier: Long-horizon and multi-agent plain-flow settings lie in a high-gain region where relative quality improvements dominate realized coordination cost increases. In short-horizon or strong-temporal baseline settings, gains remain positive but move toward diminishing-return regions.</p>
